artboards.title: New connection — step 1, pick an engine

annotations.text: The complaint was internal consistency, not direction: "nothing looks the same between 2 things". So the fix starts here — one type scale, one spacing scale, five control heights, thirteen primitives, sixteen laws. Every artboard on this canvas loads this exact stylesheet, so nothing on them can drift from it.

Read the screens as a set. The tab strip, view header, toolbar row, table and status bar are the same objects everywhere — only the verbs inside them change per engine. Every view reports its own progress in its own toolbar: a ring and an elapsed time next to the button that started the work.
No custom title bar — macOS draws it. Panel toggles moved to the right of the status bar next to Settings, icon-only, behind a hairline: things you toggle are never mixed with things you read.
Stop now sits immediately after Refresh in every view, always present — greyed when idle, red while running. Cancelling is in one place instead of appearing only once work starts.

Connection colours were re-derived: oklch(0.72 0.09 h), eleven evenly-spaced hues plus a near-neutral grey. One lightness, one chroma — no connection can shout louder than another, and there is nothing to turn up or down. Most connections have none: no colour is the default, and the 2px rail slot stays reserved either way. The rail caps the view's toolbar, not the panel — the tab strip above it belongs to several connections at once. Section 02 shows before and after.
Adding a connection is two steps now. Step 1 is a grid of engines with icons; step 2 is a dialog carrying only that engine's fields — no "Kind" dropdown, no fields belonging to another database.

Two different empties. "No tab open" keeps the workbench and lists only the tables you had open recently — one column, nothing invented. "First run" has no tree to fall back on, so the engine picker is the page.

The toolbar sheet is the proof: data, filter and search bands in every state, then the six view toolbars stacked so their identical left edge is visible at a glance. The filter row is permanent — Clear, never close — and search only ever walks the rows already fetched.
